newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY-ALL BLACKS FEAR WOUNDED SPRINGBOKS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY-ALL BLACKS FEAR WOUNDED SPRINGBOKS.

text.p: The fiercest rugby rivalry in the world invests the one-off test match between South Africa and New Zealand at Ellis Park on Saturday with an extra dimension.
The two sides who contested the 1995 Rugby World Cup final are locked at 22 wins apiece, with three games drawn, in a series that began in 1921.

South African coach Carel du Plessis is well aware of the importance of Saturday's match. He said: "The mere fact that we are playing our greatest rivals is a big influence on our preparation for this match."
"Matches between the Springboks and the All Blacks have traditionally been to decide who is the best in the world and the more experienced players in our side are very well aware of that."

But New Zealand coach John Hart said that the deadlocked series was an irrelevance. "This is a one-off test match and that is the way we have prepared for it. None of the players has even mentioned the fact that the series is currently level."
Hart criticised du Plessis for published remarks accusing the All Blacks of professional fouls. "He's jumped on the (Australian coach) Greg Smith bandwagon.

"The All Blacks do not go out to commit professional fouls and in fact if I look back to our series against the Springboks last year it was they who resorted to killing the ball to stop us from playing the game at pace."

Hart admitted that his team were probably the underdogs despite their brilliant run of test results this year. "The Springboks have picked a very heavy, very physical team and I expect them to come at us with everything. The game will be won and lost up front.

"I think the All Blacks are a slightly better side than last year because guys like Christian Cullen and Justin Marshall have had a year at the highest level. But I also think the Springboks are better, particularly amongst the forwards."

New Zealand have the luxury of fielding seven of the pack which contested the World Cup final. South Africa have made four changes up front from the side which beat the British Lions at Ellis Park two weeks ago and only Ruben Kruger and Mark Andrews remain from the World Cup final.

But the Springboks have lost only twice in seven matches at Ellis Park since readmission in 1992. One of those defeats was to the 1992 All Blacks but last year, after surrendering the series, Gary Teichmann's men gained a modicum of revenge with a 32-2 defeat of the men in black.

Hart may believe his team to be the underdogs because of the venue and the hectic travel itinerary they have undertaken. But the fact is that they carry too much firepower for anyone in world rugby at the moment and their status as unofficial world champions should be underlined on Saturday.

South Africa - 15-Russell Bennett, 14-Andre Snyman, 13-Percy Montgomery, 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Pieter Rossouw, 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen, 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Krynauw Oto, 3-Marius Hurter, 2-Naka Drotske, 1-Os du Randt.

New Zealand - 15-Christian Cullen, 14-Jeff Wilson, 13-Frank Bunce, 12-Lee Stensness, 11-Tana Umaga, 10-Carlos Spencer, 9-Justin Marshall, 8-Zinzan Brooke, 7-Josh Kronfeld, 6-Taine Randell, 5-Robin Brooke, 4-Ian Jones, 3-Olo Brown, 2-Sean Fitzpatrick (captain), 1-Craig Dowd.
